title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of type 2 diabetes and peripheral neuropathy.

History of Present Illness
The patient presents for routine follow-up. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and associated peripheral neuropathy. On examination, the provider reviewed the current management plan. The provider specifically noted that the peripheral neuropathy is considered unrelated to diabetes. The patient reports adherence to his current medication regimen, which includes insulin and metformin.

Medication List
Insulin (dosage TBD), Metformin (dosage TBD)

Exam
Vitals stable. Neurological exam reveals objective findings consistent with peripheral neuropathy. Skin exam is unremarkable apart from findings related to established neuropathy.

Assessment
1. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Stable on current regimen.
2. Peripheral Neuropathy: Stable; noted by provider as unrelated to diabetes.

Plan
Continue current regimen with insulin and metformin for management of type 2 diabetes. Follow up as scheduled. Will continue to monitor peripheral neuropathy.
explanations: The provider states the polyneuropathy is not diabetic: code diabetes without complications and the polyneuropathy separately.
Polyneuropathy not due to diabetes is coded separately (G62.9 when no cause is specified).
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Documentation of another cause overrides the 'with' presumption.
The polyneuropathy still needs its own code.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
